newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real ends steady in sluggish trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real ends steady in sluggish trade.

text.p: Brazil's real ended flat at 1.0211 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market in sluggish trade ahead of the municipal elections Thursday, traders said.

Dealers also attributed today's slow trade to a limited bank strike which began last week. Once again some banks could not participate in the forex market because their back-offices were not operating, they noted.
During afternoon session, the Central Bank bought dollars at 1.01210 real per greenback at an auction to maintain trading within the current miniband between 1.021 and 1.026 real per dollar.
Preliminary figures for commercial and financial foreign exchange contracts showed a Tuesday surplus of $ 264 million, a banker said.
In the interbank foreign exchange floating rate market, the real dropped 0.01 percent to end at 1.0267 real per dollar.
In the illegal parallel market, the real rose 0.10 percent to close at 1.039 real per greenback, traders said.
